requests.ask: Write Exit 99 (motorik / krautrock, 118 bpm, E minor, 64 bars): one unchanging beat, two interlocking picking lines, an eighth-note bass, a hook that appears and leaves, a pad in the second half; use saturate .6, packs rooms with the hall impulse at size .4, enter/exit bars instead of extra sections, duck bass and pad under the kick at depth .4, driven bass with its fundamental at 65-100 Hz, a one-source kit from the catalogue words, every note written

changes.why: kit LinnDrum: the catalogue words wanted kick tight deep click, snare medium snap noisy, hat tight bright; LinnDrum's three voices score best from one source (kick tight mid click 0.21 s, snare medium deep snap noisy, Hat Closed-03 tight bright click), Linn9000 the runner-up
sawtooth>square: the lint flagged two raw saws (bass and pad) in one section; a driven square keeps the bite and leaves the saw to the pad

.5>.3: the hook and the pad shared the mid band (masking .60 in the measure); an octave down (E3 B3) took it to .18 and the worst pair is now the guitar against the hook at .46, on opposite sides of the stage
.5>.4: two tones, E and B, an open fifth; the G is the guitar's and the hook's
.45>ramp(.4,.62): the only peak the brief allows, the hook at its brightest in bars 41-48 just before it leaves

requests.ask: It's boring. Make it hypnotic, not boring: keep the pulse constant, not the music. A distinctive riff in the first ten seconds, a second picking line that transforms how the riff feels, a memorable hook with anticipation and resolution, a bass with personality, at least one moment where the arrangement opens up, saturation and dirt and contrasting timbres; a slightly dirty electric guitar for picking A and a synth pluck for B

changes.why: form 2 sections>4 (out 24, rise 16, open 8, back 16): the first version's two 32-bar sections held the pulse and everything else still; the arc read 25/28 and the render's level moved under a dB across the song. Now 21/38/53/28, with enter/exit still carrying the entrances inside each section

arpeggio>riff: picking A is a dirty electric guitar (gm_overdriven_guitar, lpf 2800) playing a two-bar riff with rests on the and of 1 and on 3, E G A B up and D B A G E down, so there is a riff in the first ten seconds and gaps for the kick and the pluck

triangle>FM square through a dotted-eighth echo: the pluck carries the C and F# the riff lacks, six notes of three eighths each, so every bar the riff is coloured differently; in open it moves high (E5 D5 B4 D5 G5 E5)

one bar>two bars with the E3 pop: '<[0 0 0 0 2 0 4 2] [0 0 0 0 2 0 4 7]>', velocity accents 1 .7 .85 .7 1 .7 .9 .75; rise ends its second bar 7 0 2 0 4 3, open pops the octave on the beat with a sixteenth pickup
4 bars>8 bars, patch warm: a question (B4 D5 E5 G5, then a climb to B5 that stops on E5) and an answer (the same climb, down through D5 B4 G4 to E4); the warm ladder drive gives the saw its edge

the moment it opens: crash, ride on the eighths, kick pickup, harmony i@2 VI@2 i@2 VII@2 (the only chord move in the song), pad up an octave, three tones, jux wide and bright, handchimes counter-line on the hook's rests, swell at its loudest
noise swell: filtered white noise rising and falling over sixteen bars under the rise, open and back (gain 0..0.4, lpf 400..3500)

from the measure: the first measure had drums 2 dB under the mix and the riff, hook and pluck 14-20 dB under, the swell at -38; now drums .6 (open .5), riff 1.6, pluck 1.3 (open 1.4), hook 1.3 (open 1.5), handchimes 1.7, swell 1 (open 1.2), open pad .4; open: drums -2.4, riff -11.4, hook -10.9, pluck -13.3, chimes -15.5, swell -21.6; mix lint clean
.3>-.5: the pluck sits right (pan .83), so the counter-line goes left
